reference: GNU coreutils df, executed by the harness with the same Bash script and fixture-relative working directory. Runnable output is compared byte-for-byte. Contract expectations are the Bash builtin type/help metadata published for df.
coverage: Bash recognizes df as a builtin and exposes its documented help text.
GNU parity for stable filesystem type, target mount point, and input file fields on a relative fixture operand.
Filesystem type inclusion and exclusion filters on the fixture filesystem.
Diagnostics and status for invalid output fields and a zero block size.
Nested relative operands, symlink resolution, invalid comma lists, zero-size spellings and filtered missing operands.
exclusions: No operand enumerates the sandbox mount table, whose contents depend on the controller environment.
Space and inode counters, human-readable rounding, block-size arithmetic, and totals need stable statvfs data; the harness does not provide a deterministic statvfs fixture.
No host/system paths, mount operations, real network filesystems, or privileged setup are used.
The suite exceeds the preferred case count to retain the original metadata and seven operation cases while isolating regressions and two deferred gaps.
The case count exceeds the preferred range to preserve existing cases and isolate additional boundaries and regressions.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata identifies df as a builtin with PATH-independent availability.
Bash help exposes the df interface documented by the builtin.
cases.stdout:
df: df [FILE]
    Report filesystem disk space usage.
    
        bashdf [-ahHiklmPT] [-B SIZE] [-t TYPE] [-x TYPE] [FILE...]
    
        -a   show all filesystems
        -h   human-readable sizes (powers of 1024)
        -H   SI human-readable sizes (powers of 1000)
        -B SIZE  scale block output by SIZE (for example 1, K, M, G)
        -i   list inode usage
        -k   1024-byte blocks (POSIX default)
        -m   1M-byte blocks
        -l   limit listing to local filesystems
        -P   POSIX output format
        -t TYPE  limit listing to filesystem type
        -T   print filesystem type
        -x TYPE  exclude filesystem type
        --help     show usage and exit
        --version  show version and exit
        --all         show all filesystems
        --human-readable  human-readable sizes (powers of 1024)
        --si            SI human-readable sizes (powers of 1000)
        --block-size=SIZE  scale block output by SIZE
        --output[=LIST] select output columns (source,size,used,avail,pcent,target,...)
        --total       show a grand-total row
        --local       limit listing to local filesystems
        --type=TYPE   limit listing to filesystem type
        --exclude-type=TYPE  exclude filesystem type
        --print-type  print filesystem type
    
    No FILE: enumerate /proc/mounts. Pseudo-filesystems
    (proc/sysfs/cgroup/etc.) are filtered out.

cases.purpose: The fstype output field for the fixture's current filesystem matches GNU df without comparing live size counters.
The target field reports the mount point containing the relative current-directory operand.
The file field retains the relative operand (.) rather than replacing it with the containing mount point.
Use the reported filesystem type as the filter, then verify that --type retains the matching relative operand's mount target.
Use the reported filesystem type with --exclude-type and compare GNU's result when the only operand is excluded.
An unknown --output field must be rejected with a diagnostic and GNU's failure status.
A zero --block-size is invalid and must fail with a diagnostic.
Both mount target and exact operand are checked byte-for-byte on a nested relative file, dot components, and symlink; no counters are compared.
cases.script:
mkdir -p fixture/sub; : > fixture/sub/item; ln -s sub/item fixture/link
for operand in fixture/sub/item fixture/sub/../sub/item fixture/link; do
 df --output=target "$operand"
 df --output=file "$operand"
done
operand=fixture/long-name-long-name-long-name-long-name-long-name-long-name-long-name-long-name-item
: > "$operand"
df --output=file "$operand"

cases.purpose: A filesystem type absent from the private fixture excludes the only operand and emits no table.
Invalid output lists, including empty tokens, must each fail before producing a table.
cases.script:
for fields in '' source, ,target source,,target; do
 rc=0; df --output="$fields" . || rc=$?
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
done

cases.purpose: All supported argument spellings reject a zero block size with status 1 and no table.
cases.script:
for option in '--block-size=0' '-B0'; do
 rc=0; df "$option" . || rc=$?
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
done
rc=0; df -B 0 . || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
rc=0; df --block-size 0 . || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]

cases.purpose: A missing relative path must report failure even when a type filter is present.
Select only the mount target from the POSIX table using stable field parsing; counters are read but never compared. Mount identity remains byte-exact.
cases.script:
out=$(df -P .)
row=${out#*$'\n'}
read -r source size used avail percent target <<< "$row"
printf "%s\n" "$target"

cases.purpose: Check no-operand inventory and interactions among --all, --local, --type, and --exclude-type across multiple filesystem kinds.
Verify block and inode counters, -h/-H rounding, -B/-m scaling, and --total arithmetic at controlled boundary values.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r5: f_bavail < f_bfree needs a filesystem with reserved blocks (F2 ext4 mount); not authored
